summary: A research group wants to compare MIR ATR and fluorescence information on model biological tissues (chicken muscle, fat, liver) in a laboratory classification study, and asks for a first comparison experiment plus a clear statement of what its results would demonstrate.

facts_stated.text: A research group is evaluating a spectral measurement interface.

customer_premises.claim: A first comparison experiment can be designed now and its results can be stated in advance as demonstrating something clear.
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: We need a first comparison experiment and a clear statement of what its results would demonstrate.

customer_premises.claim: Heterogeneity means sequential measurements may not sample the same location, which is taken as a defining constraint of the comparison.
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: the material is heterogeneous and sequential measurements may not sample the same location

unknowns: What is being classified and into which classes (tissue type, pathology, other)?
Which fluorescence target/indicator or intrinsic fluorophores are relevant, and excitation/emission wavelengths?
Which MIR ATR wavelength range and which spectral features are expected to be informative?
Optical behaviour of each tissue type (scattering, absorption) at the wavelengths of interest.
Sample presentation: contact geometry, pressure, temperature, sample freshness/preparation.
How heterogeneity will be handled: number of measurement spots, replicates, spatial registration between MIR ATR and fluorescence.
Required classification accuracy and how performance will be validated (reference labels, cross-validation design).
Whether a fiber link is involved or the interface is bench-top contact.
Acceptance criteria for what the comparison experiment must demonstrate.
